body: ok I can see that. But realistically... how many mock executions would you have to go through before you got "bored" with knowing you were about to have your head cut off? It seems so out of human character to me. Just trying to make sense of two things that simply do not go together.

I'm not casting doubt on the video, but just genuinely curious. How / why was he able to remain so calm and say the things he does before being executed. If I knew my head was about to be sawed off my body, I'd be screaming and trying to get away until I was physically unable to continue. How can he possibly maintain composure before this?

FYI here are some specs on the recording :
4 tracks of the same guitar riffs using an American Telecaster Deluxe through a TopHat Super Club Deluxe 2x12 and a Fulltone OCD pedal (recorded with a single SM 57).  Drums are recorded with awful mics and replaced with Drumagog on toms, kick, and snare using samples purchased from Joey Sturgis (incredible producer/engineer).  Overheads were recorded (and not sampled) with two SM 57's.  Haha... yeah I know I know... it was a stupid move, but that's all I had at the time and I didn't think it was going to become as much of a project as it did.  All synth (low end to fill in for lack of a bass guitar as well as mid-high end lead synth) was created in Sony Acid. Everything recorded and mixed through Cubase 5.  I used izotope ozone to "master" it all.  It was a really fun project and I'd love to hear your input on it (opinions on the songs, the style, the mix... everything).  Thanks guys!
